findings.detail: Tasks 5-7 (Code/Security/Test Audit) and Task 8 (Pre-deploy QA) are engineering process tasks not traceable to a user-spec requirement and have no entry in User-Spec Deviations. They are acceptable as standard engineering additions (not new user-facing functionality) but their presence in Implementation Tasks makes them visible scope items without explicit acknowledgment.
findings.recommendation: keep — acceptable engineering additions. Optionally add a note in User-Spec Deviations: '[TECHNICAL] Audit tasks (5-7) and Task 8 pre-deploy QA are standard engineering process, not user-facing scope'.

findings.detail: Solution section describes at-most-once in one sentence without detailing the ordering between enroll side-effect and claim-conditional advance, or what happens on crash between enroll and advance. Architecture §How it works does not elaborate. The EMIT_EVENT precedent justifies the approach, but the ordering is not explicit enough for an L-size engine feature.
findings.recommendation: adjust — in §How it works add: 'enroll виконується ПЕРЕД claim-conditional advance; crash між enroll і advance → retry робить enroll no-op через re-enter guard; at-most-once зберігається'.

findings.requirement: Decision 5: field naming targetEntryStepId vs targetStepId in code-research
findings.detail: code-research uses targetStepId throughout (§5, §10 Quick reference). Task 4 includes code-research.md in Files to read. Task 1 description explicitly warns about this discrepancy ('code-research місцями пише targetStepId — використовувати targetEntryStepId, Decision 5'). Task 3 also warns ('НЕ targetStepId як у code-research — див. Decision 5'). However Task 4 description does not contain this warning — only Task 1 and Task 3 do. A frontend developer reading only Task 4 and code-research could use the wrong field name.
findings.recommendation: adjust — add to Task 4 description: 'code-research вживає targetStepId — використовуй targetEntryStepId відповідно до Decision 5'.
